messages:
emma_support: FYI customer AcmePay hit SSO failures right after our scheduled cert rotation (03:00 UTC). ACS callback getting 403. They say it worked before rotation. Can someone triage?

marta_idp_ops: Which errors are they seeing? Any SAML debug from our side (validation errors) or IdP side?

emma_support: Customer sent us this SAML error snippet from our logs: 
```
SAML Validation failed: Assertion recipient mismatch. expected=https://acme.example.com/saml/acs got=https://acme.example.com/saml/acs/
Signature OK. Cert thumbprint changed: 3A:4F:9B:...:C2
```
They also forwarded IdP metadata we pulled: EntityDescriptor entityID changed to "https://idp.example.com/alias" (was previously https://idp.example.com). Not sure if that alias plus trailing-slash on ACS caused recipient mismatch.

kai_eng: Quick checklist: 
- Check our idp metadata cache for AcmePay tenant (id: t-acme-01). key: idp_metadata:t-acme-01
- Force metadata refresh if the IdP repointed to a new URL that returns 200+gzip but with stale headers (If-Modified-Since causing 304).
Commands: 
```
# force refresh from internal tool
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood.local/admin/metadata/refresh?t= t-acme-01&force=1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
# view current cached entityID
redis-cli GET idp_metadata:t-acme-01
```
Also check auth-service logs for the exact VerifyLibrary error (InvalidRecipient vs AudienceMismatch). The trailing slash difference will fail strict recipient checks.

lee_sre: We saw a spike of InvalidRecipient errors on auth-service around 03:05 UTC, matching rotation. Two possible quick mitigations: 
1) Add canonical ACS variants to tenant config (add both with and without trailing slash) so assertion Recipient will match.
2) If IdP can re-issue metadata without alias or ensure the EntityDescriptor entityID remains stable, prefer that.
If needed we can rollback the cert rotation (ops) while IdP fixes metadata, but that's last resort.

marta_idp_ops: Confirmed: our metadata fetcher fetched the new metadata (served at 02:58 UTC). The IdP team added an alias EntityDescriptor for backwards compatibility and signed the metadata with the new cert. Our cache obeyed ETag and returned 304 earlier for a different path — looks like partial caching race. I'm re-pushing a metadata-only refresh and will remove alias in next IdP release.

emma_support: I asked customer to try one immediate change: update their ACS URL in the SP configuration to exactly match the logged Recipient (with trailing slash) or vice versa. I also asked them to wait while we force refresh.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: auth-service@2026.03.17-03:10 rolled out to prod (no config changes). :white_check_mark:

lee_sre: After force refresh and a small config add for the ACS alias, auth-service started accepting assertions for t-acme-01. Customer tested end-to-end and got 200 on ACS POST. Recommend monitoring for 24h for any replay issues.

emma_support: Customer confirmed SSO now succeeds. They've asked for a postmortem note on what made the alias slip through caching. I'll open a ticket for improved metadata freshness checks and a fallback to accept exact-ACS variants when a new cert is detected. :thumbsup:

marta_idp_ops: Filing ticket: IDP-OPS-482: "prevent alias-only EntityDescriptor rollouts without tenant compatibility check". Will coordinate with IdP partner.

emma_support: Closing this thread for now — marking resolved and moving to follow-up doc for postmortem/change request. Thanks all. :handshake:
